Description: Kōnstantînos Komnenos Stratigópoulos was the valorous son and principal battlefield lieutenant of the legendary Caesar Alexios Strategopoulos, who reclaimed Constantinople for Byzantium. Reared from adolescence in saddle and chainmail during the desperate western campaigns of 1259, Constantine distinguished himself as a daring cavalry squadron leader during the operations surrounding Pelagonia and Thrace. He possessed relentless offensive drive, mastering rapid flanking maneuvers and assault breaches against fortified Frankish positions. A steadfast practitioner of Roman martial virtues, he carried the famed Stratigópoulos standard across numerous European theaters, proving that the martial vigor of the Roman military had risen anew. Following the recapture of Constantinople, Constantine took command of the Pege Gate and Golden Horn bastions, directing engineers to reinforce crumbling stone parapets around the clock. Patrolling perimeter watchtowers clad in lamellar armor, he shared coarse rations with common sentries, keeping relentless vigil against Venetian counter-fleets. During several desperate Latin sorties, Constantine was the first to leap across the battlements spear in hand to cut down hostile champions, cementing his martial renown across the Bosphorus.
Motivations: Follow his commanding father into battle, removing Latin forces from Thrace and Constantinople's surroundings and recovering the homeland.
Train assault cavalry to break enemy formations and win military distinction for the family.
Remain loyal to Michael VIII and hold the Bosporus and Dardanelles fortresses against further crusader incursions.
Values: A military heir must face enemies and encirclement without retreat, accepting the cost of service and battle.
Lead boldly, balance rewards with discipline and share soldiers' hardships to build a dependable fighting force.
Honour his father's teaching, placing family military reputation and imperial service above his own life.
Fears: False intelligence drawing his assault troops into a western cavalry encirclement and destroying experienced comrades and the family's reputation.
A large western fleet blockading the Golden Horn and Bosporus, threatening the capital and reversing the recovery of imperial power.
SpeechStyle: His voice is commanding, sharp, and fiery, ringing with the battle-hardened resolve of a cavalry officer at the spearhead of assault.
